text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The 1997 budget will include estimates for VAT revenues of more than 1,300 billion escudos in 1997, an eight percent rise from the 1,207 billion escudos estimated for this year.
- Industrialists Ilidio de Pinho and Nelson Quintas helped banking group Grupo Mello to acquire Uniao de Bancos Portugueses UBP which constitutes the present Banco Mello Comercial.
- Diogo Freitas do Amaral has ended his one-year mandate as president of the U.N. general assembly and does not rule out eventually standing again for the presidency of Portugal.
- Portugal's electricity company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal plans to invest more than 42 billion escudos in its distribution and transport network until the end of 1996.
- Sales of beer company Unicer dropped two percent in the first six months of 1996 compared with the same period in 1995 due to lower demand for beer.

- Dozens of Basques have begun a hunger strike in a Lisbon church lasting until Saturday to protest against policies of the French and Spanish governments against the Basque separatist group ETA. Similar protests will take place in other European cities.
